title: Ask Your Meetings: Get Answers From Your Own Meeting Notes | Ask Lynkk

lines: You had the answer once.
Someone said it in a meeting, three weeks ago.
A start date. A budget. A promise to send something by Friday.
Now nobody can find it.
Most of what a team decides is said out loud, in meetings.
Afterwards, it sits in recordings nobody rewatches, in notes spread across different places, and in people's memory.
So you scroll through transcripts, ask a colleague, or book another meeting to go over the last one.
Decisions get made twice. Promises slip.
The notes exist.
What's missing is a way to ask them a question.
That's what Ask Lynkk is for.
Lynkk records your meetings and writes the notes: a transcript with speaker labels, key takeaways, decisions, open questions, and action items with an owner and a due date.
Ask Lynkk is a chat that answers only from your own notes. It's part of Lynkk Pro.
It starts with the meeting.
Record a call with the Mac app or the Chrome extension, and no bot joins it.
Or send the meeting bot to Google Meet, Zoom and Teams.
For a meeting in person, record your mic in the browser at lynkk.ai.
Then ask in plain words.
What did Acme say about the renewal?
Ask Lynkk finds the right notes by person, company or project, and answers with citation chips that show where each part came from.
Open the evidence, and the note plays from the moment it was said.
Ask what's still open.
It lists the open tasks and decisions across your notes.
Search looks at meaning and keywords together, so you don't need the exact words someone used.
You can attach a file to the chat: a PDF, a Word document, text, Markdown or a CSV.
And you can act on the answer.
Create a Google Calendar event with a Meet link, share a note, mark a task done, or create a Jira issue.
Every action waits for you on a confirm card.

scenes.chapter: Before the meeting, and in Slack
lines: It helps before a meeting, too.
Connect Google Calendar, and on days you have meetings, Lynkk emails you a morning briefing: who you're meeting, your most recent note with them, and how many action items are still open between you.
And in Slack, ask the Lynkk app a question and get an answer from your notes, with sources and a button to open it in Lynkk.
Here's how people use it.
In sales, ask what a customer said about the renewal before the next call.
In product and engineering, ask why a decision was made, then send the tasks to Jira from the note, one issue each.
Managers ask what they promised in each one-on-one.
And in a team workspace of up to 10 seats, everyone gets Pro, so everyone can ask their own notes.
Answers come only from your own notes.
Transcripts cover 17 languages, four of them in beta.
Recordings are private to your account, and Lynkk never trains on your conversations.
Stop searching your meetings. Ask them.
Start free at lynkk.ai.
